# ethereum-optimism/ethereum-optimism.github.io Monthly Report (February 2026)

## 🚀 Highlights
In February 2026, development focused on expanding the Superchain ecosystem's asset diversity and strengthening the repository's foundational documentation. Significant effort was directed toward integrating new tokens (RNBW, OLAS, XAN) and refining schema validations for emerging chains like Ink and Swellchain. Beyond asset management, the team engaged in deep technical discussions regarding `op-supernode` architecture, specifically addressing state synchronization and "Safe" label management to ensure protocol security as interop features mature.

## 🛠️ Key Developments

### Ecosystem Expansion & Token Integration
The repository saw a steady influx of new assets and network support, reflecting the growth of the Superchain.
*   **New Token Support:** Integrated several new tokens including RNBW ([#1264](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/ethereum-optimism.github.io/pull/1264)), OLAS on Celo ([#1258](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/ethereum-optimism.github.io/pull/1258)), and XAN ([#1266](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/ethereum-optimism.github.io/pull/1266)).
*   **Data Hygiene:** Refined the token list by removing duplicate entries for LDO ([#1273](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/ethereum-optimism.github.io/pull/1273)) and updating circulating supply figures ([#1277](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/ethereum-optimism.github.io/pull/1277)).
*   **Network Mapping:** Updated the `L2_TO_L1_PAIR` mapping to include missing chains, ensuring accurate cross-layer tracking ([#1270](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/ethereum-optimism.github.io/pull/1270)).

### Infrastructure & Schema Validation
To maintain data integrity across an increasing number of chains, the team updated core validation logic.
*   **Schema Updates:** Added support for Celo, Celo Sepolia, Swellchain, Ink, and Ink Sepolia to the `TOKEN_DATA_SCHEMA` validation array ([#1269](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/ethereum-optimism.github.io/pull/1269)).
*   **Website Structure:** Added a new `index.html` file, signaling foundational updates to the project's web presence ([#1265](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/ethereum-optimism.github.io/pull/1265)).

### Documentation & Contributor Experience
Efforts were made to streamline the onboarding process for new developers and improve public-facing documentation.
*   **Guidelines:** Introduced a `CONTRIBUTING.md` file to standardize the contribution process ([#1274](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/ethereum-optimism.github.io/pull/1274)).
*   **Maintenance:** Performed various "housekeeping" tasks, including fixing grammar in CircleCI configs ([#1271](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/ethereum-optimism.github.io/pull/1271)) and correcting subject-pronoun agreement in the README ([#1272](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/ethereum-optimism.github.io/pull/1272)).

## 🐛 Issues & Triage

### Resolved Issues
*   **L1 Polling:** Fixed a critical bug where HTTP L1 URLs caused virtual nodes to stop polling, which previously led to stale L1 head updates ([#19012](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/ethereum-optimism.github.io/issues/19012)).
*   **Interop Testing:** Closed an issue regarding skipped acceptance tests for interop proofs, though technical debt remains regarding specific TODOs in the codebase ([#18616](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/ethereum-optimism.github.io/issues/18616)).

### Active Technical Discussions
*   **`op-supernode` State Management:** Significant debate continues regarding how the Consensus Layer (CL) and `op-supernode` manage "Safe" labels. The goal is to prevent deadlocks by ensuring the CL remains the sole controller of the engine while the virtual node handles interop-specific logic ([#18976](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/ethereum-optimism.github.io/issues/18976)).
*   **Flashblocks Support:** Discussions are underway to merge Flashblocks support into `op-geth`. This integration aims to reduce disk space requirements compared to archive nodes by processing events via Websockets ([#756](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/ethereum-optimism.github.io/issues/756)).
*   **Sync Correctness:** The team is investigating `op-node` behavior during initial Execution Layer (EL) sync, specifically how to ensure the node does not prematurely mark blocks as finalized during Snap Sync ([#17631](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/ethereum-optimism.github.io/issues/17631)).

## 💬 Community & Collaboration
The month was characterized by high engagement in protocol-level architecture. Contributors like **sebastianst** provided critical insights into CI failures related to RPC calls in `superchain-ops`, suggesting infrastructure-level fixes for block range errors ([#17688](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/ethereum-optimism.github.io/issues/17688)). The collaborative effort to refine the withdrawal process in the ETH bridge tutorial also highlighted a need for better validation alignment between the Optimism SDK and third-party tools like Viem ([#1956](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/ethereum-optimism.github.io/issues/1956)).
